:::{#thm-affine-map-zero}
#### An affine map sends zero to its offset

An affine map $f(\vx) = \matr{A}\vx + \vec{b}$ (@def-affine-map)
satisfies $f(\vzero) = \vec{b}$.

:::

::: proof

First, $\matr{A}\vzero = \vzero$: for each $i$,

$$
\ba
(\matr{A}\vzero)_i
&= \sumjp a_{ij} \cd 0
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\&= \sumjp 0
&& \text{(any number times } 0 \text{ is } 0 \text{)}
\\&= 0
&& \text{(a sum of zeros is } 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

Then

$$
\ba
f(\vzero)
&= \matr{A}\vzero + \vec{b}
&& \text{(@def-affine-map)}
\\&= \vzero + \vec{b}
&& (\matr{A}\vzero = \vzero)
\\&= \vec{b}
&& \text{(adding } \vzero \text{ changes no entry; @def-vector-addition)}
\ea
$$

:::
